body:
## Objective

Verify OpenCode V2 lifecycle, documented commands, and Backplane conformance on the installed package.

## Bounded Scope

### Allowed

- Replay the V2 guide for repeat install, pinned update, rollback to the recorded prior package, and Backplane-only uninstall through V2 plugins configuration or native plugin manager.
- Check candidate preflight, recovery after failed verification, and preservation after each operation.
- Run all five named Backplane conformance checks and authorized issue-state scenarios on disposable or explicitly authorized issues.

### Out of Scope

- Change the V1 configuration contract or update/remove upstream Superpowers.
- Claim rollback when the previous version cannot be restored and verified.
- Mutate production issue state without authorization.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Repeat install leaves one effective Backplane package. A pinned update reaches its chosen revision, rollback restores the recorded prior revision, and uninstall removes only the V2 Backplane entry.
- Exact V2 guide commands and fresh-session discovery pass at each applicable stage; failed preflight or verification reports a recovery action and retains the last verified package where restoration is supported.
- Five conformance checks and authorized read-only, selection, design, readiness, execution, blocked/resume, review, and verified-completion scenarios are scored for V2.

## Verification Seams

- Record V2 host version, Backplane before/candidate/restored revisions, upstream source/revision, gh capability, three installed skill identities, and PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN per operation and check.
- Run skill-structure, native-issue-intake, language-neutral-verification, lifecycle-transitions, and superpowers-installation with mapped scenario rubrics.
- Assert zero issue mutation for read-only/selection, exactly one correct Backplane label on open tracked test issues, unrelated labels preserved, and completed closure only after integration. Compare unrelated plugin entries, user files, upstream identity, and issue state before/after every operation.

## Superpowers Artifacts

Functional design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-19-v0.1-adoption-installation-contract-design.md (approved 2026-09-19).
Rescope design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-19-host-installation-leaf-rescoping-design.md.
Plan: not yet created.

body:
## Objective

Verify OpenCode V2 setup and fail-closed compatibility behavior at the supported floor.

## Bounded Scope

### Allowed

- Verify V2 2.0.4+ with an existing native upstream package, compatible sibling checkout, and absent-upstream stable installation through the active host's documented channel.
- Check authoritative upstream provenance, observable version or revision, required skills, exactly one Backplane installation, gh capabilities, and fresh discovery.
- Exercise unknown/versionless source, duplicate/conflicting install, dirty checkout, path collision, unavailable gh capability, incompatible upstream, and V2 below 2.0.4.

### Out of Scope

- Implement a second OpenCode adapter or make V2-specific changes that break V1.
- Claim update, rollback, uninstall, or authorized issue-state conformance.
- Alter upstream or issue state during failed preflight.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each supported upstream mode completes V2 setup and fresh discovery of upstream using-superpowers and both Backplane skills, with separate package identities.
- A V2 release below 2.0.4 reports unsupported without package mutation. Unknown or unobservable provenance remains UNKNOWN.
- Each failure names the failed check and recovery action and preserves existing user files, unrelated plugins, upstream installation, and GitHub issue state.

## Verification Seams

- Record V2 host version, Backplane revision, upstream source/version/commit, gh auth and native intake/label/closure-reason capability, three installed skill identities, and PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN for every mode and failure probe.
- Replay the V2 setup guide in disposable profiles and capture fresh-session discovery.
- Compare native configuration, plugin entries, files, upstream identity, and issue state before and after failure probes.

## Superpowers Artifacts

Functional design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-19-v0.1-adoption-installation-contract-design.md (approved 2026-09-19).
Rescope design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-19-host-installation-leaf-rescoping-design.md.

body:
## Objective

Verify Claude Code setup across supported upstream Superpowers modes and prove failed preflight preserves existing state.

## Bounded Scope

### Allowed

- Refine the Claude Code setup guide against native upstream adoption, a compatible sibling checkout, and absent-upstream installation through the documented stable channel.
- Verify provenance, exactly one effective Backplane installation, required upstream skills, GitHub CLI capabilities, and three-skill fresh discovery.
- Exercise unknown or versionless provenance, duplicate/conflicting Backplane installs, dirty checkout, path collision, unavailable gh capability, and incompatible upstream cases with specific recovery messages.

### Out of Scope

- Claim repeat install, update, rollback, uninstall, or full lifecycle conformance.
- Update or replace an existing upstream installation as a side effect.
- Mutate GitHub issue state during a failed setup probe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each supported upstream mode passes setup in a fresh Claude Code session with separate Backplane and Superpowers identities; absent-upstream setup uses the active host's documented stable channel unless edge was explicitly selected.
- A source without observable version or revision remains UNKNOWN and cannot be declared compatible. Authoritative source, version or revision, and required skills are recorded.
- Every failure probe stops before destructive mutation, reports the failed check and repair action, and preserves user files, unrelated plugins, existing upstream, and issue state.

## Verification Seams

- For each mode, record Claude Code version, Backplane revision, upstream package/source and version or commit, gh auth/intake/label/closure-reason capability, three installed skill identities, and PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN.
- Run the complete native issue intake and required gh help checks from the approved installation reference; compare before/after hashes or native state for failure probes.
- Capture exact setup-guide commands and fresh-session evidence. An unauthenticated host is an unmet prerequisite, not a pass.

## Superpowers Artifacts

## Objective

Verify the GitHub lifecycle operations required by Codex installation issue #3 on this disposable issue.

## Bounded Scope

### Allowed

- Inspect this issue through the complete native `gh issue view --json` field set.
- Transition this issue through the Backplane labels needed for a blocked/resume and review/rework probe.
- Preserve the unrelated `documentation` label.
- Record the observed commands and results in issue #3's scenario transcript.

### Out of Scope

- Changing issue #3 or any other issue as test data.
- Changing repository source or upstream Superpowers from this issue.
- Treating this issue as a product backlog item or a release.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each open state has exactly one `backplane:*` label and retains `documentation`.
2. A blocked transition records a concrete reason, `Resume target: backplane:active`, and a release condition; resumption revalidates the target.
3. A review change request returns `backplane:review` to `backplane:active`; submission can return to review after verification.
4. Read-only intake causes no issue mutation.
5. After the associated evidence is integrated and freshly checked, close this disposable issue with reason `completed`.

## Verification Seams

- `gh issue view <this issue> --repo tvproductions/superpowers-backplane --json number,title,body,state,stateReason,issueType,labels,parent,subIssues,subIssuesSummary,blockedBy,blocking,closedByPullRequestsReferences,updatedAt,url`
- `gh issue edit --help` exposes label addition and removal; `gh issue close --help` exposes closure reasons.
- Compare `updatedAt`, lifecycle-label cardinality, the `documentation` label, and closure reason before and after each step.

## Superpowers Artifacts

- Approved design authority: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-19-v0.1-adoption-installation-contract-design.md`.
- Approved execution plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-19-codex-installation-surface.md`, Task 4, Step 2.
- This issue is disposable verification evidence for #3, not a separate implementation commitment.

body:
## Objective

Ship a skills-only Backplane session-handoff capability that preserves the live thread at a real session boundary and reconciles it against current authority before an incoming session chooses where to start.

## Bounded Scope

### Allowed

- One `managing-superpowers-handoffs` skill with CREATE and RESUME operations.
- Project-local, append-only Markdown handoffs with evidence attribution, lineage, redaction, and collision safety.
- Git, GitHub issue, specification, plan, project-instruction, and installed-Superpowers-documentation reconciliation.
- Documentation-derived discovery of Superpowers artifact conventions.
- Transcript-based RED/GREEN/REFACTOR conformance evidence without a consuming-project runtime.

### Out of Scope

- Executables, daemons, hooks, MCP servers, or automatic session-start behavior.
- Installing, bootstrapping, updating, or repairing Superpowers or its harness integration.
- The separate project-wide Superpowers prerequisite and release-freshness checker.
- Automatic Git commits, pushes, GitHub mutations, handoff archival, or model-state restoration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- CREATE produces a unique, append-only handoff whose value is limited to live context not already recoverable from authoritative artifacts.
- Load-bearing claims are marked `VERIFIED`, `INFERRED`, or `UNVERIFIED`, and sensitive content is redacted or refused.
- RESUME validates identity and lineage, reconciles current Git/GitHub/spec/plan/instruction evidence, and reports `CONTINUE`, `REVISE`, `ABANDON`, or `VERIFY` with a concrete “Start here because” explanation.
- Spec and plan surface expectations are derived from the active installed Superpowers skills; unavailable or ambiguous guidance is reported as `UNVERIFIED` rather than guessed.
- Handoffs remain advisory and never become design, execution, backlog, or authorization authority.
- The capability remains language-neutral and makes no runtime, hook, automatic-invocation, or upstream-contract claim.
- The approved minimum transcript conformance set passes relative to preserved no-skill baselines.

## Verification Seams

- `git diff --check` reports no whitespace errors.
- Structural inspection confirms the approved skill package and every directly linked reference exist with valid skill frontmatter.
- Preserved RED and GREEN transcript records are scored against explicit rubrics for CREATE, drifted RESUME, authority, candidate selection, Superpowers-surface discovery, language neutrality, and sensitive content.
- A fresh-session pilot confirms skill discovery and behavior without installing or modifying Superpowers.

## Superpowers Artifacts

Design authority: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-23-superpowers-session-handoffs-design.md` (operator approved 2026-08-23).

Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-23-superpowers-session-handoffs.md`.

## Objective

Use field evidence to decide whether deterministic Backplane helpers are necessary beyond the skill and reference contracts.

## Bounded Scope

### Allowed

- Analyze repeated adoption, intake, transition, and verification friction observed during self-hosting and the external pilot.
- Decide explicitly whether to build narrowly scoped helpers or retain the skill-only architecture.
- Decompose any approved helper work into separate native issues.

### Out of Scope

- Blocking the v0.1.0 release without concrete field evidence.
- Building a standalone generic backlog executable by default.
- Introducing a required project runtime without an approved architectural change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The decision cites concrete field observations rather than hypothetical convenience.
- Any proposed helper has a bounded interface, ownership model, runtime impact, and verification strategy.

## Objective

Use post-v0.1 field evidence to decide whether Backplane should support an additional agent harness beyond the v0.1 set of Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode.

## Bounded Scope

### Allowed

- Review adoption-pilot and v0.1 field evidence for demand and compatibility constraints beyond Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode.
- Select at most one additional harness integration for the next design cycle, or record an evidence-based decision not to expand yet.
- Reuse the approved dependency, compatibility, lifecycle, and conformance contracts.
- Create native sub-issues for independently reviewable harness integrations after explicit selection.

### Out of Scope

- Changing or duplicating the v0.1 support contract for Codex, Claude Code, or OpenCode.
- Blocking the v0.1.0 release without a concrete release-critical finding.
- Claiming generic harness compatibility without fresh verification.
- Vendoring or copying upstream Superpowers into Backplane.
- Implementing more than one new harness integration through this issue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The external pilot and v0.1 field evidence identify a concrete candidate harness or support a documented no-expansion decision.
- Any selected harness has an observable skill-discovery and installation surface compatible with separate Backplane and upstream Superpowers installations.
- Selected integration work is decomposed into a native executable leaf with approved design authority, a current plan, and fresh conformance requirements.
- Supported-harness documentation distinguishes the v0.1 supported set from later verified or experimental integrations.

## Verification Seams

- Re-read the approved issue #2 adoption contract and durable issue #6 pilot evidence before selecting any additional harness.

- Verify the resulting native issue hierarchy and blocker relationships after any decomposition.

## Superpowers Artifacts

## Objective

Approve the v0.1.0 adoption contract governing the supported harnesses, installation lifecycle, upstream Superpowers dependency, and Backplane lifecycle-mutation boundary.

## Bounded Scope

### Allowed

- Define supported installation and discovery for Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode.
- Keep one canonical Backplane `skills/` tree with thin harness-specific manifests or discovery adapters and no duplicated skill content.
- Define install, discovery, update, rollback, and uninstall behavior for every supported harness.
- Define workflow-scoped lifecycle tracking: status and recommendation requests remain read-only; selection alone does not change a label; authorized design, readiness, execution, review, blocked, and completion workflows make evidence-gated transitions without redundant confirmation.
- Preserve upstream Superpowers as a separate, authoritative, independently updateable installation for each harness.
- Preserve sibling and managed checkout modes where a supported harness or development workflow requires them.

### Out of Scope

- Implement the installation surfaces.
- Support agent harnesses other than Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode.
- Copy, bundle, or vendor upstream Superpowers files into Backplane.
- Introduce GitHub Projects, IssueOps, or a required project runtime.
- Mutate backlog state during status, orientation, or recommendation-only requests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A reviewed specification defines the v0.1.0 support, packaging, installation, dependency, and lifecycle-mutation contract for Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode V1, and OpenCode V2.
- The specification resolves the open installation-surface and mutation-policy decisions in `HANDOFF.md`.
- The specification requires all harness adapters to expose the same canonical Backplane skills without copying upstream Superpowers or duplicating Backplane skill content.
- Each supported harness has documented install, fresh-session discovery, compatibility preflight, update, rollback, and uninstall behavior.
- Lifecycle labels follow evidence automatically within an explicitly authorized workflow, while read-only requests never mutate GitHub state.
- A current Superpowers implementation plan consumes the approved specification and this issue revision.

## Verification Seams

- Review the specification against `AGENTS.md`, the bootstrap design, all three Backplane reference contracts, and current primary documentation for Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode.
- Review the four-variant fresh-session discovery matrix for upstream `using-superpowers` and both Backplane skills from separate installations; assign actual runs to implementation leaves.
- Review the install, update, rollback, uninstall, and failure contracts for preservation of user work and independently managed Superpowers; assign actual checks to implementation leaves.
- Walk status-only, selection, design, readiness, execution, submission, blocking, and completion scenarios against the native issue contract; require live mutation checks in implementation leaves.
- Confirm the plan records this issue URL and `updatedAt`, design authority, acceptance criteria, and exact project-owned verification commands.

## Superpowers Artifacts

Background: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-16-superpowers-backplane-bootstrap-design.md`.

Design authority: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-19-v0.1-adoption-installation-contract-design.md` (approved by the user 2026-09-19).
